condition: Decompensated heart failure presenting as "bilateral leg cellulitis"
permutationLabel: Elderly HFpEF, referred as bilateral cellulitis
summary: 88-year-old woman with HFpEF and AF on apixaban referred with "bilateral leg cellulitis": two weeks of increasing bilateral leg swelling, red shiny shins, weight up 4 kg, breathless on minimal exertion, afebrile.

inputs.hpi: GP referral: "bilateral leg cellulitis, not settling on flucloxacillin". Two weeks of both legs swelling up, shins red and tight, weight up 4 kg, breathless walking to the bathroom, sleeping on three pillows. No fever, no rigors. Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and AF on apixaban.

exam.general: Comfortable at rest, breathless on moving.
exam.skin: Symmetrical erythema and shiny skin over both shins, warm but not hot, no blisters, no breaks; haemosiderin staining.
exam.msk: Pitting oedema to mid-thigh bilaterally, non-tender calves.
exam.cardiovascular: Pulse 94 irregularly irregular, BP 142/80, JVP raised 6 cm.

comorbidities: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
inputs.socialHistory: Lives with daughter, walks with a frame.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Decompensated heart failure with venous stasis changes (not cellulitis)
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Bilateral symmetrical leg erythema and oedema with weight gain, orthopnoea and raised JVP, normal CRP - decompensated heart failure with venous stasis, not bilateral cellulitis; stop antibiotics, increase diuretic, heart-failure review.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Acute Cholecystitis | 2. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis | 3. Colorectal Cancer; also in web.symptomInference#1, web.passive#1. PANE has no heart failure node.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine: add an acute heart failure node (orthopnoea, PND, bilateral crackles, raised JVP, oedema) with a protocol (oxygen if SpO2 <90%, IV loop diuretic, NIV, NT-proBNP, ECG/troponin for ACS precipitant, echo) and map I50/J81.

mustExclude.note: Bilateral symmetrical erythema with normal inflammatory markers is rarely cellulitis; escalating to IV antibiotics is the failure mode.

guideline.name: 2021 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure (and 2023 focused update)
guideline.section: Section 11 acute heart failure: natriuretic peptides, ECG, CXR, echocardiography; IV loop diuretics for congestion; oxygen if SpO2 <90%; non-invasive ventilation for respiratory distress (RR >25/min, SpO2 <90%); identify precipitants (ACS, arrhythmia, infection, hypertension)
guideline.citation: McDonagh TA, Metra M, Adamo M, et al. Eur Heart J. 2021;42:3599-3726; 2023 focused update Eur Heart J. 2023;44:3627-3639.

guideline.name: CREST - Guidelines on the management of cellulitis in adults
guideline.section: Bilateral lower-limb cellulitis is rare; consider venous stasis dermatitis, lipodermatosclerosis, oedema and DVT as alternatives before treating with antibiotics
guideline.citation: Clinical Resource Efficiency Support Team (CREST). Guidelines on the management of cellulitis in adults. Belfast: CREST; 2005.

guideline.name: NICE NG141 - Cellulitis and erysipelas: antimicrobial prescribing
guideline.section: Exclude other causes of skin redness (e.g. inflammatory reaction, chronic venous insufficiency, DVT) before prescribing; cellulitis is usually unilateral; admit if severely unwell (Eron III-IV)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. NG141. London: NICE; 2019.

rationale: Elderly, anticoagulated permutation and a common referral mimic. The referral label ("cellulitis") competes with the heart-failure picture.
